episode_title: ✅ JENSEN IS BACK - Tech Selloff: Crash or Opportunity? My Strategy for When to Buy, Hold & Sell

real_qa.q: What is the host's strategy for when to buy, hold, and sell stocks during a tech market selloff?
real_qa.r: The host uses tools and charts to make informed decisions rather than timing the market. He sold out of positions on Thursday to save hundreds of thousands of dollars, but remained partially invested. His strategy includes tracking momentum through relative performance indicators in TrendSpider, monitoring the fear and greed index, and considering historical patterns like the 2018 midterm correction that resulted in a 20% drop followed by a nearly full rebound by Q1.
real_qa.requete: stock market strategy buy hold sell

real_qa.q: What does the S&P 500 moving average pattern suggest about current market conditions?
real_qa.r: The S&P is now 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, which is only supposed to happen once every 190 years. Since 1950, this has occurred in 1987, 2011, and 2015, all of which turned out to be great buying times. The host describes this as potentially a generational buying opportunity, referencing how investors who bought Amazon or Google during the 2003 tech drawdown would have benefited significantly.

real_qa.q: What is the current Fear and Greed Index reading compared to historical levels?
real_qa.r: The Fear and Greed Index today is at 11, down from 18 the previous reading and 37 one week ago. One year ago, it was at 5, meaning current conditions match the same position from last year. The host uses this metric alongside the VIX and bond rates as indicators for potential buying opportunities.
real_qa.requete: Fear and Greed Index current reading

real_qa.q: How did the QQQ index perform after the market crash in April 2023?
real_qa.r: On April 4th, the VIX reached 45, which was a moment of significant fear. The QQQ index went on to achieve a 14% gain from that low point. The host uses this historical example to illustrate how market fear can present buying opportunities for investors willing to act when others are afraid.

real_qa.q: What specific tools does the host recommend for stock analysis without relying on general internet AI?
real_qa.r: The host recommends Sidekick, TrendSpider, and Seeking Alpha's AI tools because they operate as walled gardens that do not pull from general internet sources. He states these tools very rarely give false answers. He also highlights his own resources including Daily Stock Pick app with a free Receipts tool and his Substack newsletter, all accessible through Linktree, as trusted places for stock analysis.
real_qa.requete: Sidekick TrendSpider Seeking Alpha stock analysis
